name: ODYSSEY 08 · A DAY FOR SONGS AND CONTESTS

rows.t: Sing, Demodocus! Sing the famous quarrel — Odysseus and Achilles, best of the Achaeans, at strife with high words at the gods' rich feast!

rows.t: Rest the lyre — we have had our fill of feast and song. Out to the games now, all of you, that our guest may tell his people at home how far we surpass all men at boxing, wrestling, the jump, and the race!

rows.t: So the whole company pours out from the hall at the king's heels, toward the marked field of contest.

rows.t: The youths of Phaeacia rise up: they run and the dust hangs over the plain, they wrestle, they leap, they hurl the discus, they trade blows in boxing.

x_odyssey.speaker: PERFORMER.NARRATOR

x_odyssey.direction: names each contest as it flashes past
x_odyssey.delivery: frame the action without replacing character agency

rows.t: Come, father stranger, try our games yourself — you have the build of an athlete under those griefs. No fame in a man's life is greater than what his own hands and feet win him.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.laodamas
x_odyssey.payload: Laodamas invites Odysseus
x_odyssey.direction: steps forward courteously with the invitation
x_odyssey.delivery: courteous prince inviting participation and later supporting reconciliation
reveal: Laodamas invites Odysseus

rows.t: No, I see no athlete here. A master of cargoes, rather — one who minds his freight and his greedy profits. Nothing of the games in him.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.euryalus
x_odyssey.payload: Euryalus insults him as a merchant without athletic skill
x_odyssey.direction: smirks for the crowd's benefit
x_odyssey.delivery: talented youth whose careless insult triggers the demonstration
reveal: Euryalus insults him as a merchant without athletic skill

rows.t: That was badly spoken, young man, and it stings me to my feet. See where the stone flew — past every mark of yours, and I threw it clothed and weary. Now let any Phaeacian but Laodamas, my host's son, come and try me — boxing, wrestling, or the race, I refuse no one.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.odysseus
x_odyssey.payload: Angered, Odysseus hurls a discus beyond every mark and challenges the athletes
x_odyssey.direction: seizes the greatest discus and hurls it whistling beyond all the marks
x_odyssey.delivery: reluctant injured guest becoming sharply competitive after insult
reveal: Angered, Odysseus hurls a discus beyond every mark and challenges the athletes

rows.t: Peace, stranger — no man of sense could fault your worth. Watch now what we do best, for in swift ships and the running foot, in dance and song, we lead all men.

x_odyssey.payload: Alcinous calms the confrontation and shifts the display toward dance and song
x_odyssey.direction: calms the field and signals for dancers and lyre
x_odyssey.delivery: derive from current embodied condition and relationship pressure
reveal: Alcinous calms the confrontation and shifts the display toward dance and song

rows.t: Hear now how Ares and golden Aphrodite lay together in secret, and how the lame smith Hephaestus forged a net fine as spider-thread that no eye could see, and caught the lovers fast in his own bed till all the gods stood laughing at the door.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.demodocus
x_odyssey.payload: Demodocus sings how Ares and Aphrodite were trapped in Hephaestus's invisible net
x_odyssey.direction: sings to the lyre while the circle dances
x_odyssey.delivery: derive from current embodied condition and relationship pressure
reveal: Demodocus sings how Ares and Aphrodite were trapped in Hephaestus's invisible net

rows.t: Alcinous, you boasted your dancers were the best beneath the sun, and here the boast stands proved. Wonder takes me as I watch — their feet flash and my eyes cannot follow.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.odysseus
x_odyssey.payload: Odysseus praises their unmatched movement
x_odyssey.direction: genuine awe, freely given
x_odyssey.delivery: derive from current embodied condition and relationship pressure
reveal: Odysseus praises their unmatched movement

rows.t: Then the twelve lords bring gifts for the guest — fresh-washed cloak and tunic and a talent of precious gold from each — and the heralds carry all before the queen.

x_odyssey.speaker: PERFORMER.NARRATOR
x_odyssey.payload: The nobles offer gifts
x_odyssey.direction: measures out the wealth of the giving
x_odyssey.delivery: frame the action without replacing character agency

rows.t: Farewell, father stranger — if a harsh word was spoken, let the storm winds snatch it up and carry it away. Take this sword of bronze, silver on the hilt, the sheath new-carved ivory, and may the gods grant you your home and your wife.

x_odyssey.delivery: pride softened into formal apology and gift transfer

rows.t: Demodocus, above all mortals I honor you — the Muse taught you, surely, or Apollo, for you sing the Achaeans' fate as though you stood among them. Take this cut of honor from my own portion. Now shift your ground and sing the wooden horse, the trap Epeius built with Athena, that noble Odysseus led up into Troy filled with fighting men.

rows.t: Stop the lyre, Demodocus — not all here take joy of it, for since the song began our guest has not once left off weeping. Now, stranger, hide it no longer: tell me the name your father and mother called you, and your land and your city. And say why you weep at the doom of the Argives and Troy — did some kinsman fall there, or a comrade dear as a brother?
